simple.meaning: עֲנָיָה (ʻĂnâyâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “Anajah , the name of two Israelites.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עֲנָיָה (H6043) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Nehemiah 8:4, with occurrences in Nehemiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲנָיָה (H6043) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עֲנָיָה (H6043) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עֲנָיָה (ʻĂnâyâh) / H6043 is traced through Nehemiah 8:4, Nehemiah 10:23 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: Anajah , the name of two Israelites
definitions.full: H6043. Anayah עֲנָיָה proper name, masculine Neh 8:4 ; 10:23 , Ανανια ( ς ). עָנָיו see עָנָו below III. ענה . עָנִים . עִנְיָן see [II. ענה ]. עָנֵם see גְּנִּים עֵין .

occurrences.englishText: Ezra the scribe stood on a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
